BOUNDARY: The empty-carrier case is excluded because a cluster point exists (the hypothesis provides a point). In a one-point space, any proper filter is both Cauchy and convergent to the point, and the proof holds. The nonempty choice in step 1.2 is guaranteed by the cluster‑point definition. Potential counterexamples (e.g., the right‑neighbourhood filter on ℝ) satisfy the lemma; a Cauchy filter on an incomplete space without a cluster point does not meet the hypothesis. The proof does not rely on any hidden separation, metric, or completeness assumptions.
